categoryD_examinationAndCertificationCon.description: Statutory examination entry, promotion, and pass certificate criteria.
criteria: Minimum six registered external examination subjects
At least five subjects passed individually, including English, with minimum 33% marks for the Pass Certificate
Attainment of at least Grade D (lowest passing grade) in SUPW & CS; Grade E is failing and precluding Pass Certificate

Examination Entry Attendance (Chapter I, Section E): Minimum 75% attendance of working days in each year of the two-year course. Discretionary condonation authority is vested in the Chief Executive and Secretary for shortages between 60% and 74.9% (illness or special circumstances) and for shortages below 60% in exceptional cases (serious psychological/medical grounds, authorised sports/arts representation, unforeseen circumstances). Condonation is discretionary, not an automatic entitlement.

Class IX Promotion (Chapter II, Section B, clause 4): Internal school promotion; minimum 33% marks in 5 subjects individually including English; minimum 75% attendance of working days; no other criteria permitted

Class IX Subject Change Cutoff (Chapter II, Section B, clause 3): Candidates shall not be permitted to change subjects after 15 September of the year in which they were registered in Class IX (cutoff: ${class9RegistrationYear}-09-15). Clause 3 establishes this prohibition after the cutoff date; procedural requirements for changes on or before the cutoff date are unspecified by Clause 3.
Class IX-to-Class X Subject Continuity: Candidate entering Class X may not opt for a subject for which they were not registered and studied in Class IX
School Subject Provision: School may not enter candidates for subjects for which the school makes no provision

curriculumFrameworkProfiles.sourceDocument: NCF-SE 2023 (Part A, Sections 2.4.3, 3.4.6.3, 3.5.3.2) & CBSE Circulars Acad-15/2026, 18/2026
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.curricularStructureCitation: NCF-SE 2023 Part A, Section 2.4.3 (Middle Stage, printed p. 51): curricular expansion to Sciences, Social Sciences, Vocational Education exposure, subject-specific learning and inquiry.
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.assessmentGuidanceCitation: NCF-SE 2023 Part A, Section 3.4.6.3 (Assessment across Stages: Middle Stage, printed p. 87): competency-based assessment covering all learning dimensions; classroom techniques include projects, debates, presentations, experiments, investigations, role plays, journals, portfolios; regular summative assessments at logical intervals; periodic assessments with MCQs and constructed responses; comprehensive summative assessment of competencies in each area by end of Middle Stage.
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.timeAllocationCitation: NCF-SE 2023 Part A, Section 3.5.3.2 (Time Allocation for Middle Stage): R3 Language introduced in Middle Stage.
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.inclusionCriteriaRationale: Covers supplementary co-curricular, skill and exposure areas (Kaushal Bodh, CT & AI, Art Education, Physical Education) while core academic disciplines (Science, Math, Social Science, Language) are represented in the canonical curriculum catalogue.

curriculumFrameworkProfiles.name: CISCE Upper Primary (Classes VI–VIII) Curricular Framework Profile
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.governingAuthority: Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.sourceDocument: Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI–VIII), First Edition, November 2016
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.frameworkCurricularAreas: 7 subject areas (English, Second Language, Mathematics, Science [Physics, Chemistry, Biology], History/Civics & Geography, Computer Studies, Arts Education) + 4 additional curricular areas (Third Language Classes V–VIII, Physical Education / Yoga, Education in Moral and Spiritual Values, SUPW)
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.assessmentGuidance: Prescribes continuous school-level formative and summative evaluation across syllabus themes; CISCE does not prescribe statutory council-level assessment percentages or board examination rubrics for Classes VI–VIII.
curriculumFrameworkProfiles.educationInMoralAndSpiritualValuesRation: Education in Moral and Spiritual Values is preserved as an institutional framework area under Upper Primary 2016 but excluded from grade-specific individual assessment entries because it represents a school-wide values/ethos curriculum without independent grading or exam rubrics.
